version.changelog:
## playwright-browser-use 1.0.16 Changelog

- Removed redundant documentation file: `skill-card.md`
- No functional changes; all core features and behaviors remain unchanged.

llm.summary: The skill is openly described as a powerful browser automation tool, but default mode gives one local daemon token broad code execution, session credential, file upload, and persistent browser authority.

dimensions.detail: The tool is proportionate for trusted, visible local automation, but safe mode does not appear to restrict arbitrary destination navigation or local file upload paths, leaving internal-resource access and host-file disclosure risks for less-trusted agent use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is conventional Node/npm with a pinned package-lock dependency on playwright-core and a local shell wrapper; I did not find automatic remote payload execution. A fallback npx browser-install suggestion is documented but not part of automatic install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documentation discloses the attack surface and recommends safe mode, but high-impact commands are enabled by default and there is no enforced per-action confirmation or per-capability authorization boundary.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The daemon intentionally persists browser state across commands, stores its bearer token in ~/.pw-browser, supports credential export/import by default, and keeps command history with raw non-token parameters that may include secrets.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The browser automation purpose is coherent, but the default capability set includes arbitrary page JavaScript, daemon-side custom Playwright code, direct cookie/localStorage read-write, arbitrary navigation, upload/download, and authenticated browser actions under a single token.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only for trusted local use where you can see and interrupt the browser. Prefer starting the daemon with PW_BROWSER_SAFE_MODE=1 for agent-driven or untrusted-page workflows, use PW_BROWSER_CRED_PERSIST=off if session files should never be written, avoid using it on sensitive logged-in accounts, and clear cookies/storage plus shut down the daemon when finished.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] expected: The eval and run-code surfaces are real and disclosed as advanced automation features, but their default availability and full browser-session authority justify Review rather than malicious classification.
[RA2] expected: Cookie and storage export/import are documented session-management features with path and mode mitigations, but they still create reusable credential material and persistent privilege risk.
[T05] expected: The static concerns about broad default privilege, unrestricted navigation, credential access, and file upload are supported by the artifact; these are purpose-aligned but under-scoped for untrusted or prompt-driven use.
[T09] expected: Custom code execution and operation history are documented features, but Node vm is not a strong hostile-code boundary and history stores raw parameters beyond the daemon token.
[TM1] unexpected: The curl -k text is a dependency security explanation, not an executed command, and the rm -rf example targets a specific daemon state file for troubleshooting; I did not treat this as a material standalone issue.
[AE1] unexpected: The referenced artifact was available in the workspace and I inspected the required SKILL.md plus referenced documentation, so this scanner concern was overridden.
[SQP-3] unexpected: SKILL.md is Chinese, but English README and quickstart files are included and the language limitation is disclosed; this is not a main driver of the verdict.
[RP1] unexpected: The unpinned npx text appears as a fallback human instruction for installing a browser if none exists, not as automatic runtime behavior.
